articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and Job Design: A Dynamic Framework
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study aims to deepen the understanding of artificial intelligence's (AI) impact on work by introducing and describing the AI-Job Dynamics Framework. articles.title: Situating Vulnerability: An Ethical Governance Framework for Anthropomorphic AI Interaction
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly address users in the register of care: they remember personal details, adopt a first-person emotional voice, and sustain relationships across many sessions. articles.title: The Privacy Paradox Is a Misnomer: Data Under Structural Uncertainty
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The infamous privacy paradox refers to the apparent inconsistency between people's stated concern for privacy and their readiness to disclose personal information. This phenomenon has sparked two largely disconnected literatures: one offering experimental evidence of inconsistent behavior, and another providing qualitative accounts and defending the importance of privacy. The Article presents an online field experiment that bridges those literatures and shows that the so-called paradox arises from a mischaracterization of the underlying behavior.

articles.title: Privacy Preference Controls for Agentic Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In response to vast and widespread online tracking, regulators and technologists alike have worked to develop laws and tools that allow people to express their privacy preferences. These measures seek to offer users greater control over the sale and sharing of personal information, putting agency in their hands to protect their privacy. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Our position shifts the target of peer-review reform from reducing uncertainty through evaluator improvement or judgment aggregation to constraining evaluative authority under persistent uncertainty. Scientific peer review aims to assure research quality but also allocates scarce academic opportunities, such as publication in high-impact venues. articles.title: AI Security Literacy: Ecosystem-based Competency Framework and K-12 Learning Platform
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adoption of artificial intelligence in K-12 schools has outpaced guidance for students, teachers, and administrators. articles.title: From Canon to Nikon: Camera Domain Shift and Potential Equity Implications in Retinal AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.29104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet access to regular screening remains limited worldwide. AI offers a scalable approach, but its performance can be sensitive to image quality and acquisition conditions.
